settings.fromASpeedTest: Measure upload speed on your server's internet connection, not on a remote phone. Remote streams share 80% of it.
settings.letYourHouseholdAnd: Let your household and friends sign in from outside your home.
settings.yourHomeSOutside: Your home's outside address couldn't be found.
settings.yourRouterIsBehind: Your router is behind another router or your provider shares addresses, so people outside may not reach Arc even with the port forwarded.
settings.arcAnsweredAtIts: Arc answered at its outside address.
settings.openThePortOn: Open the port on the router
settings.askingLetSEncrypt: Asking Let's Encrypt for a certificate…
settings.theCertificateIsFetched: The certificate is fetched on the first visit to the domain.
settings.offAwayFromHome: Off: away from home, passwords and what you watch travel unencrypted. Turn it on before sharing your address.
settings.onTheSamePort: On the same port as plain HTTP. At home both work; people away from home are sent to HTTPS.
settings.aDomainNamePointing: A domain name pointing at your home's address (a free dynamic DNS name works). Let's Encrypt checks it on port 443, so set the outside port to 443.
settings.privateKeyFilePem: Private key file (.pem or .key), full path
settings.pemFilesReadAgain: PEM files, read again whenever they change, so another tool can renew them.
settings.checkError: {{error}}. Many routers can't reach their own outside address from inside the home, so try it on a phone with Wi-Fi off.
settings.forwardDescription: Forward port {{outside}} on your router to port {{inside}} on this computer, in the router's settings.
settings.outsidePortDescription: The port people away from home connect to. Usually the same as Arc's port ({{port}}); Let's Encrypt needs 443.
settings.networksDescription: Extra networks to treat as home, like a VPN or Tailscale ({{network}}).
settings.movedAddress: Arc has moved. <address>Open it at its new address</address>.
settings.trustedProxiesDescription: If you reach Arc through a reverse proxy like SWAG or Nginx Proxy Manager, add its address so people at home count as home.

devices.itCanBeSigned: It can be signed out again in Settings > Devices.
devices.showingTheLastLoaded: Showing the last loaded devices. They may be out of date.
devices.description: Signing in an Arc app on a TV or another device? Enter the code it shows.

importDialog.waitingForYouTo: Waiting for you to sign in to Plex…
importDialog.approveArcMediaServer: Approve Arc Media Server in the Plex tab that opened, then come back here.
importDialog.thisRunsInThe: This runs in the background; you can close this and follow it in Activity.
importDialog.plexOpensInA: Plex opens in a new tab so you can sign in and let Arc read your server. Your password never passes through Arc.
importDialog.anAdministratorCanRead: An administrator can read everyone’s watch history. The password is only used to sign in and isn’t kept.
importDialog.whichPlexServerShould: Which Plex server should Arc import from?
importDialog.watchedResumePointsRatings: Watched, resume points, ratings, history, watchlist and playlists
importDialog.plexOnlyLetsArc: Plex only lets Arc read resume points, ratings, the watchlist and playlists for the account you signed in with; everyone’s watched titles come from Plex’s history. The server’s collections come over for everyone.
importDialog.doneContinueWatchingWatched: Done. Continue Watching, watched ticks and Insights now include what came over.
importDialog.plexDescription: Bring over what everyone has watched, where they stopped and their ratings, plus Plex’s watch history, watchlists, playlists and collections. Arc only reads from Plex, and never replaces newer progress in Arc.
importDialog.jellyfinDescription: Bring over what everyone has watched, where they stopped and their ratings, plus favourites, playlists and collections. Arc only reads from Jellyfin, and never replaces newer progress in Arc.
importDialog.accountsFromServer: Choose whose watch history goes to which Arc profile (from {{server}}).
importDialog.accountsDescription: Choose whose watch history goes to which Arc profile.
importDialog.listsError: Couldn’t bring the watchlist and playlists: {{error}}
